key_insight: BiSCo-LLM compresses LLM weights with a lookup-free binary spherical code and residual binary coding, targeting extreme low-bit storage without explicit codebooks.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical path to reduce model memory, bandwidth, and checkpoint size while avoiding the storage and lookup overhead of conventional vector quantization.
method: Map local weight chunks onto a unit hypersphere and binarize them into packed sign codes.
Use a residual BSQ stage to encode reconstruction error without storing codebooks.
Apply category-wise recovery distillation plus a protected 8-bit channel for sensitive weights.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an evaluated storage budget that counts binary codes, neural decoders, protected channels, LoRA adapters, and metadata, indicating a full-system compression assessment.
watch_item: The method adds decoder, protected-channel, and metadata overhead, so real compression gains depend on careful accounting and deployment implementation.
paper_title: BiSCo-LLM: Lookup-Free Binary Spherical Coding for Extreme Low-Bit Large Language Model Compression
